When we first manually purged at the start of our shift, we noticed that the pressure from the return pump was abnormally low. The first shift operator reported that the Russel Finex had become clogged, so they left the return pump on Manually while they purged and got chocolate flowing again. This appears to have drained the enrober enough to cause the low pressure we saw. The production line for the Dark Truffle chocolate is operating stably, with no deviations to report. The capture test was successfully passed, and both the components and ingredients were verified. The tempering process is within the specified ranges, the metal detector is checked hourly, and the product weights have been fine-tuned to meet the target. The screening system and its filters are in good condition, with no issues. The organoleptic properties of the product—including its appearance, aroma, flavor, and texture—are excellent. The flow-wrapping process is well-controlled, with a pack count of 250 to 270 pieces per box; this, combined with the final palletization, meets all requirements set forth in the product specification.
